Compound $PdC{l}_{4}. 6{H}_{2}O$ is a hydrated complex; 1 molal aqueous solution of it has freezing point 269.28 K. Assuming 100% ionization of complex, calculate the molecular formula of the complex
( ${K}_{f}$ for water = 1.86 K kg $mol^{- 1}$ )
questions.solution:
$\Delta T = i \times {K}_{f} \times m$
$( 273 - 269.28 ) = i \times 1.86 \times 1$
$3.72 = i \times 1.86$
$i = 2$
$\alpha = \dfrac{i - 1}{n - 1}$
$1 = \dfrac{2 - 1}{n - 1}$
or $n = 2$
Thus, the complex should give two ions in the solution, i.e., the complex will be $[ Pd ( {H}_{2}O{)}_{3}C{l}_{3} ] Cl. 3{H}_{2}O$.

According to van't Hoff equation
$\text{Osmotic pressure} \left(\text{\pi}\right) = \text{i CRT} = \dfrac{{\text{in}}_{\text{B}} \text{RT}}{\text{V}}$
i = 2.47; V = 2.5 L; R = 0.0821 L atm K-1 mol-1
T = 27 + 273 = 300 K; π = 0.75 atm
${\text{n}}_{\text{B}} = \dfrac{\text{\pi} \text{V}}{\text{iRT}}$
$= \dfrac{\left(\text{0.75 atm}\right) \times \left(\text{2.5 L}\right)}{\left(\text{2.47}\right) \times \left({\text{0.0821 L atm K}}^{- 1} {\text{mol}}^{- 1}\right) \times \left(\text{300 K}\right)} = \text{0.0308 mol}$
Amount of CaCl2 dissolved = nB × MB
= (0.0308 mol) × (111 g mol-1)
= 3.42 g

questions.q:
At 300 K, 36 g of glucose present in a litre of its solution has an osmotic pressure of 4.98 bar. If the osmotic pressure of the solution is 1.52 bar at the same temperature, what would be its concentration?
[Report your answer upto two decimal places.]
questions.solution:
$\text{\pi} = \text{CRT} = \dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{V}}$

For both solutions, R, T and V are constants.

For I solution

$\left(\text{4.98 bar}\right) = \dfrac{\left(\text{36g}\right) \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}{\left({\text{180 g mol}}^{- 1}\right) \times \text{V}} \text{...(i)}$

For II solution

$\left(\text{1.52 bar}\right) = \dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{V}} \text{...(ii)}$

On dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (i), we get

$\dfrac{\left(\text{1.52 bar}\right)}{\left(\text{4.98 bar}\right)} = \dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{B}} \times \text{V}} \times \dfrac{\text{180} \times \text{V}}{\text{36} \times \text{R} \times \text{T}}$

$\dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{B}}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{B}}} = \dfrac{\text{1.52}}{\text{4.98} \times 5} = {\text{0.0610 mol L}}^{- 1}$
